scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.audio: Do you often regret certain decisions? Only to find out later that you overlooked some psychological traps?

scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.audio: It's like being lured by a limited-time offer on the street and rushing to buy things, only to realize later that you don't need them at all.

scenes.label: Problem Solving
scenes.audio: Many mistakes are actually false appearances provided by the environment, making us take the bait voluntarily.

scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.audio: Charlie Munger compiled the Psychology of Human Misjudgment when he was 81 years old, which was earlier than Kahneman's behavioral economics theory.

scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.audio: He used this set of thinking to avoid many major mistakes in investment decisions. Munger said, 'I'd rather gain an advantage by understanding mistakes rather than just relying on luck.'

scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.audio: Know yourself and the enemy, find out where the mistakes are first, only then is there room for correction.

scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.audio: When facing decisions, don't let psychological traps lead you by the nose. Reflect first to see if it's possible you've fallen into a misjudgment.

scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.audio: If you also want to know more about Charlie Munger's wisdom, hurry up and follow me. Bye-bye.
